title: Choosing and using ladders for trade and exterior work
audience: Trade and exterior workers who select, inspect, set up and climb ladders, and the supervisors who allow them.
learningOutcomes: Choose a ladder type and rating for a given task, load and surface.
Check a ladder before use and withdraw one that has a defect.
Set up and climb a ladder with the correct angle, landing extension and three-point contact.
Decide when a ladder is not the right tool, and when a ladder needs a fall-protection measure.

instruction.heading: A ladder is a way of getting to a place
instruction.body: A ladder gets a person to a place. It is not a good place to work from for long, and two of the sources treat ladders as a significant route into falls from elevation. This lesson sets out a decision path. First, can the task be done without climbing? Second, is a ladder suitable? Third, if a ladder is used, can it be set up and used safely? A ladder suits short, light work.

instruction.heading: Choosing the type and rating
instruction.body: Choose the type first. Step ladders and platform steps are self-supporting. Extension and straight ladders lean on a wall and need a landing point at the top. Each ladder has a rated load that must cover the worker, clothing, tools and materials together, and exceeding it can make the ladder collapse. The material matters as well. Metal conducts electricity, so metal ladders stay away from live services, and timber or fibreglass ladders are chosen for specific tasks. Read the rating label and confirm it is legible before the ladder is used.

instruction.heading: Setting up on a firm base
instruction.body: Set up on a firm, level base. Where the ground is soft or sloped, use levelling feet or do not use that ladder. Keep doors and walkways clear, or block them off. Where a ladder can be fixed at the upper end, secure it, and where it cannot be secured, have a second person foot it while the worker climbs. For a leaning ladder, use the angle the maker states. A non-Australian source also asks that the top of a straight ladder extend above the landing.

instruction.heading: Climbing and working on the ladder
instruction.body: Face the ladder, hold the stiles rather than the rungs, and keep three-point contact on the ladder at all times. Carry nothing in the hands: use a tool belt, or hoist tools with a rope once the worker is in position. Avoid overreaching; the belt buckle stays between the stiles, and move the ladder rather than leaning to one side. The highest rung of a step ladder is not a standing place. Do not climb while tired, unwell, or affected by any substance that impairs balance.

instruction.heading: When a ladder needs a fall-protection measure
instruction.body: Where the worker must lean or reach from a ladder at a working height above the trigger that the sources set, counted from the foot of the ladder to the worker's feet, one source requires fall protection where it is appropriate. The figure is non-Australian, so do not use it. One source also require a lanyard to be attached at the working height before the task begins, and released last when the worker descends. The clearer rule is this: the higher the position and the further the worker reaches, the stronger the case for a platform, a scaffold or a different method.

instruction.heading: Check before and after the work
instruction.body: Inspect the ladder before each use and again afterwards. Check the rails for bends, splits, twists or breaks. Check the rungs or steps for bends, cracks or missing parts. Check the joints, bolts, rivets and hinges for tightness, the locks, spreaders and safety bars for function, and the feet and levellers for wear. A ladder that fails any check is removed, tagged and reported. Keep inspection records for ladders in regular use.

instruction.heading: Authority to use access equipment
instruction.body: The duty to manage work at height applies in each state and territory. Some states set licence or authorisation rules for certain elevating equipment. This lesson does not state those rules. Check the rule for the state where the work happens before any ladder task is planned. This lesson does not grant any authority.

procedure: Decide whether the task can be done from the ground or with a tool that avoids climbing.
Choose the ladder type for the task, and check its rating against the total load, including tools and materials.
Inspect the ladder. Withdraw and tag it if any check fails.
Set up on a firm, level base at the maker's angle, with the landing extension confirmed.
Fix the upper end of the ladder, or have a second person foot it while it is not secured.
Climb with three-point contact, carrying nothing in the hands.
Work within safe reach, and move the ladder rather than overreaching.
Descend with three-point contact, and secure the ladder when the work is finished.

workedExamples.situation: A technician must replace a light fitting in a 3-metre ceiling, using a two-step step ladder on tiled flooring.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which checks come first, and what is the stop rule?
workedExamples.reasoning: Check the ladder and its rating, set it up on a firm base, keep the top step unused, and use a second person if the floor is uneven. The stop rule is simple: if the work needs both hands and a long reach, use a platform or a different method rather than leaning.

workedExamples.situation: A worker plans to clean a gutter from a six-metre extension ladder leaning on the fascia, with a bucket hooked on a rung.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which parts of the job are unsafe, and what should replace them?
workedExamples.reasoning: The bucket adds a load that upsets balance, the reach requires leaning and overreaching, and the fall exposure is high. The job needs a ground-based or platform method. If a ladder is still used, it needs a fall-protection measure and a second person.

equipmentAndPpe: Ladder rated for the total load, with a readable rating label
Levelling feet or stabilisers where the ground is uneven
Tool belt or hoist rope for tools and materials
Second person for footing where the ladder is not secured

commonErrors.error: Overreaching to one side of the ladder.
commonErrors.prevention: Move the ladder so the belt buckle stays between the stiles.

commonErrors.error: Carrying tools in the hand while climbing.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a tool belt, or hoist tools with a rope once in position.

commonErrors.error: Standing on the highest step of a step ladder.
commonErrors.prevention: Mark the highest permitted step, and stay below it.

commonErrors.error: Setting a ladder against a loose, moving or unsuitable surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Choose a fixed, sound point, check it, and secure the ladder.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Warning: do not use a metal ladder near electrical services or live wiring. Choose a non-conductive ladder for that work.
Warning: the rated load covers the worker, clothing, tools and materials together. Exceeding it can lead to collapse.
Use the maker's label and the Australian ladder standard once checked.
AS 1892 series (portable ladders) is listed as the Australian ladder standard family.

Licence notice: a high risk work licence applies to boom-type platforms. In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold. This lesson does not grant a licence or any authority to use access equipment at height.

qualityStandard: Ladder type and rating are matched to the task and the total load.
A pre-use inspection is recorded for each ladder.
The set-up angle and landing extension are checked and recorded.
Three-point contact are kept throughout the climb.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use inspection record for each ladder
Withdrawn ladder tag and defect report
summary: Use a ladder only for short, light work, and only after asking whether it is needed.
Check the rating, the rails, the rungs and the base before each use.
Keep three-point contact and carry nothing in the hands.
Ladder rules, licence positions and thresholds must be checked by state before use.

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker must carry a box up a ladder. What is the safe option?
options: Carry it in one hand while climbing slowly and hold the rail with the other hand while the box stays on the top rung
Hoist it with a rope once the worker is in position, and keep both hands on the ladder while climbing.
Hold it in the teeth while you climb the ladder slowly with both feet on the rungs
Throw it up onto the platform from the ground without a rope or a helper at all today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about step ladders is consistent with the sources?
options: The top step is a good standing position for reaching high ceilings for most jobs
The highest rung is not a standing place, and the worker should not stand on the top step.
Step ladders can be used without checking their rating if the ladder looks sound
Step ladders need no inspection because they are self-supporting and the feet are not checked

knowledgeChecks.question: A leaning ladder is being set up. Which check matches the sources' guidance?
options: The ladder should be placed against the nearest soft surface and it should be tied to the nearest post
Set it up at the maker's angle, on firm and level ground, with the top extending above the landing and secured where possible.
It is fine to lean it against a window frame and the frame is strong enough for the worker to climb up to the top
The ladder can be extended while the worker stands on the rungs and the top is then left free to move

officialReferences.title: Using portable ladders in the workplace
officialReferences.covers: WorkSafe Victoria guidance (Victoria only). Ladder selection considers the task (including reach), stability, height and ground conditions. For workplace use the page specifies a minimum 120 kg safe working load rating under AS 1892.1, which is named but not read. Ladders with loose, missing or damaged rungs, steps, treads or top plates must not be used. Non-slip feet and a setup area clear of other hazards are required. Three points of contact must be maintained on the ladder. For A-frame ladders, do not stand on or above the second step from the top; for straight or extension ladders, do not stand on a rung less than 1 m from the top. For access, the ladder should extend 3 rungs above the step-off point or 1 m. Not covered by this page: removing or tagging out a faulty ladder, and a requirement that the base be level. Publisher: WorkSafe Victoria.
